On the Windows box (2026-09-24, Entire CLI 0.11.0), `git commit` in any JusPrin worktree can sit forever in
`.git/hooks/prepare-commit-msg`, which runs `entire hooks git prepare-commit-msg ... || true`. Nothing is
logged to `.entire/logs/entire.log` while it waits; it seems to wait on keyboard input the agent's shell cannot give.
Two sessions hit it the same evening (the Undo commit and the setup-flow Done commit), and both sat 10-40 minutes.

**Why:** It looks like a slow checkpoint condense, so it is easy to wait a long time for nothing.

**How to apply:** Run commits in the background. If the commit has not landed after a couple of minutes, find
the `entire` process started by that commit (`ps -W | grep /entire`, check its start time) and kill only that
PID. The hook's `|| true` lets git finish, and later hooks (commit-msg, post-commit, post-rewrite) have gone through
normally. Do not pass `--no-verify`. A second commit right after (the rebase) did not hang, so it is intermittent.
See [[windows-build-machine]].

content.text:
The hook stops to ask "Link this commit to session context? [Y/n]" and waits for a keypress that can never come.

**What happens**
- When the committing session has file changes to link to the commit, `entire hooks git prepare-commit-msg <file> message` shows that prompt. That's the path `git commit -m` takes.
- It reads the answer from the Windows console directly (`CONIN$`), not from stdin, so redirecting stdin (`</dev/null`) doesn't help.
- On macOS and Linux an agent's shell has no terminal, so Entire can't open one and skips the prompt. On Windows the agent's Git Bash has a hidden console, so Entire can open it, and the read then blocks forever.
- Commits with nothing to link skip the prompt. That's why it looked intermittent, and why the retry after a rebase went through.
- Entire buffers its log, so `.entire/logs/entire.log` stays empty while it waits. That's why nothing showed up there.

**Evidence**
- **Hang reproduced:** it hung with source `message`. With no source (the editor path) it finished in 0.8s.
- **Where it blocks:** I listed the hung process's open handles. It had opened the console device and was stuck in a read on it, with no child processes and almost no CPU.
- **Entire knows about this case:** the binary contains Entire's own integration for another agent (Pi). It adds `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` to every agent bash command, and its comment says agent shells "inherit a real TTY but cannot answer" hook prompts. The Claude Code integration evidently doesn't do this.
- **The fix works:** with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, the same call finished in about 0.3s and added the `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer in 3 of 3 runs. Without it, 3 of 3 hung until killed.

**A separate problem that isn't the hang:** while the vigilant-hodgkin session's `msbuild -m` build ran, it held all 16 cores at 100%. Every program launch slowed down, and `entire version`, normally 0.2s, took 17–19s. That makes commits slow but they do finish.

**Fix options**
1. Commit as `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 git commit ...`. That works now.
2. Set it for every agent shell by adding `"env": { "GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT": "0" }` to `~/.claude/settings.json`. The side effect is that git over HTTPS will fail rather than ask for credentials; in an agent shell that ask would hang anyway. I haven't changed your settings; say if you want that.
3. Report it to Entire: on Windows, its Claude Code integration shouldn't treat an inherited hidden console as a user who can answer.
